content: Reliability coefficients are interpreted directly as the percent of variability in test scores that is due to true score variability, and when the reliability coefficient is .80, this means that 80% of variability in scores is due to true score variability and 20% is due to measurement error.
According to classical test theory, variability in test scores is due to a combination of true score variability and random error.
The multiple baseline design is the best single-subject research design for evaluating virtual reality exposure treatment for a 34-year-old woman's storm, height, and spider phobias.
The Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) can be used to estimate a test's internal consistency reliability when test items are scored dichotomously.
The Spearman-Brown formula is used to estimate the effect of adding or subtracting items on a test's reliability coefficient.
Percent agreement as a measure of inter-rater reliability may overestimate reliability because it is affected by chance agreement.
The kappa coefficient is used to evaluate the inter-rater reliability of a test when scores or ratings on the test represent a nominal scale of measurement.
Thorndike's research with cats in a puzzle box led to his development of the law of effect.

Continuing to say "I love you" to his mother whenever she yells at the boy is a result of escape conditioning, where the behavior is maintained because it allows the boy to "escape" his mother's yelling.
The standard error of measurement for a test that has a standard deviation of 10 ranges from 0 when the reliability coefficient is 1.0 to 10 when the reliability coefficient is 0.

To increase the test-retest reliability of a newly developed measure of intelligence, the test developer should increase the number of test items and make sure the new sample of examinees is heterogeneous with regard to level of intelligence.

subdomain_name: Test Validity - Content and Construct Validity
content: The multitrait-multimethod matrix is used to evaluate a test's construct validity.

subdomain_name: Test Validity - Content and Construct Validity
content: The multitrait-multimethod matrix provides evidence of a test's convergent validity when scores on the test have high correlations with scores on other tests that measure the same or a related construct.

subdomain_name: Test Validity - Content and Construct Validity
content: In a multitrait-multimethod matrix, a large monotrait-heteromethod coefficient provides evidence of a test's convergent validity.
External validity refers to the extent to which research results are generalizable to other people, settings, and times.

Cohen's kappa coefficient is the appropriate technique for determining the inter-rater reliability of the ratings made by the manager and assistant manager when they categorized employees as being ready or not ready for promotion.
When using positive reinforcement to establish or increase a behavior, use of the variable ratio schedule of reinforcement will maximize the behavior's resistance to extinction.
The analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) is used to statistically remove the effects of an extraneous variable on the dependent variable.
Adding a new selection test to the current hiring decision procedure will increase decision-making accuracy through incremental validity.
Eta is used when both variables are measured on a continuous (interval or ratio) scale and the relationship between the variables is nonlinear.
John Watson used delay conditioning to establish Little Albert's fear response to white rats.
Statistical power is increased by all factors except population heterogeneity on the dependent variable.
Ambivalent sexism, as described by Glick and Fiske's (2001) theory, consists of hostile and benevolent components of sexism.

The first stages of Atkinson, Morten, and Sue's Racial/Cultural Identity Development Model and Cross's Black Racial Identity Development Model are characterized by positive attitudes toward White (majority) culture and negative attitudes toward Black (minority) culture.

The Generations Study was a five-year study that examined the health and well-being of lesbian, gay, and bisexual (LGB) individuals who represented three age cohorts: 18-25, 34-41, and 52-59. Included in this study were questions about participants' ages when they first experienced five sexual identity milestones: awareness of same-sex attraction; self-identification as lesbian, gay, or bisexual; same-sex sexual behavior; disclosure as a sexual minority to a straight friend; and disclosure as a sexual minority to a family member. Consistent with previous research, Bishop, Fish, Hammack, and Russell found that members of the younger cohort reported first experiencing all milestones at the youngest ages, while members of the older cohort reported first experiencing all milestones at the oldest ages.
The gain-loss effect explains that people are more attracted to those who initially dislike them but then change their minds after getting to know them.

Hovland and Sears (1940) found that, as the market price for cotton decreased between 1882 and 1930 in the Deep South, the number of lynchings of African American men increased, which is best predicted by scapegoat theory.
Tajfel and Turner's social identity theory proposes that prejudice and discrimination are attributable to a natural tendency to categorize people into groups.
According to Helms's White Racial Identity Development Model, people in the contact stage have a lack of awareness of racism and White privilege and are satisfied with the racial status quo.

Consistent with previous research, the Generations Study found that members of the youngest age cohort (ages 18 to 26) reported the earliest ages of onset for all sexual identity milestones and the shortest lengths of time between milestones.

The use of hair straighteners and skin bleaching creams and social stratification based on skin tone by people of color are examples of internalized racism, which involves the internalization (acceptance) of negative messages about one's own racial or ethnic group accompanied by self-devaluation and a preference for the beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors of members of the dominant culture.
The type of microaggression where communications exclude, negate, or nullify the psychological thoughts, feelings, or experiential reality of a person of color is referred to as microinvalidation.

A White therapist in the final "autonomy" stage of Helms's model of White racial identity development has non-racist attitudes and a stable White identity not rooted in privilege, and is likely to be more effective when working with clients from racial or ethnic minority groups.
Troiden's homosexual identity development model consists of four stages: sensitization, identity confusion, identity assumption, and commitment.

According to Atkinson, Morten, and Sue's (1998) racial/cultural identity development (R/CID) model, people belonging to a racial/cultural minority group who are questioning their attitudes toward their own minority group and the majority group are in the dissonance stage of identity development.

Using the salary history of job applicants to determine the wages they offer, even though this practice results in applicants belonging to racial/ethnic minority groups regularly being offered lower wages than the wages offered to White applicants for the same job, is an example of institutional racism.

Dawis and Lofquist's (1984) theory of work adjustment is a person-environment fit theory that emphasizes the importance of the match between a person's characteristics and the characteristics of the job.

Dawis and Lofquist's theory of work adjustment identifies tenure as the primary indicator of work adjustment and proposes that it's affected by two factors - satisfaction and satisfactoriness.
Driver and Brousseau's career concept model distinguishes between four career concepts: linear, expert, spiral, and transitory.

Compared to cones, rods are more important for peripheral vision.

In Baddeley's (2000) multi-component model of working memory, the episodic buffer is responsible for integrating information in working memory with information in long-term memory.
Proactive interference occurs when prior learning (e.g., Spanish) interferes with the ability to learn or recall new information (e.g., French), as illustrated by Ella's experience.

subdomain_name: Brain Regions/Functions - Hindbrain, Midbrain, and Subcortical Forebrain Structures
content: High scores on the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale were most associated with increased volume of the striatum, which is part of the basal ganglia.

Retroactive interference, where more recently acquired information interferes with the ability to recall previously learned information, explains why you called your co-worker's husband "Bob" after earlier meeting him as "Bill".

Priming is a method for studying implicit memory, and there are several types of priming, including repetition priming, which occurs when presentation of a word or object facilitates later identification of that word or object in a different format or context, and word-stem completion and word-fragment completion are two of the repetition priming tasks that are used to investigate implicit memory.

Retrieval from long-term memory is maximized when the conditions at the time of learning (encoding) new information are the same as the conditions when the information must be recalled, as described by the encoding specificity hypothesis.
